metadata.title: A quadratic family of integral two-torsion classes in the cokernel of an explicit Koszul-strand presentation
metadata.description:
Let M_p be the explicit integral matrix of the connecting map in a lower Koszul strand of the quadratic part of the presentation ideal of the fiber cone of the conductor, in a family of Huneke-Wiegand counterexamples. For every integer p>=8 we prove that its cokernel contains a direct summand (Z/2)^floor(((p-2)^2+3)/12), indexed by the strictly increasing nonnegative triples of sum p-2. Reflection-symmetric interval potentials give explicit integral sources for twice each class; relative parity functionals supported on ten to twelve rows detect each class independently over F_2, and their extension gives a nonconstructive splitting. A previously tracked four-row vector is integrally congruent to one triangle class.

For a semantic projection retaining four of six recurring row types, a face classification of one source column proves that two endpoint triangle rows vanish for every p>=8. Exact computations test each identity: complete F_2 row-span certificates for all 27 triangles at p=8,...,12, 586 endpoint identities through p=300, and a finite carrier comparison at p=8,...,11. That M_p presents the stated strand is a premise, machine verified for p=8,9,10 and conjectural for larger p. The complete cokernel, an upper bound, and a uniform comparison with isolated subpresentations remain open.

Son Pham retains priority for the original public Huneke-Wiegand counterexample. Source code, computation records and archived sources: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH .
metadata.version_notes: Revision. New: a problem-and-context section (the conjecture and its disproofs by Pham and by Christensen-Gerko-Iyengar, the Koszul complex, strand and module that the matrix presents, and what integral two-torsion says about the characteristic dependence of the Betti numbers); a related-work section on algebraic Morse theory, matroids over rings, FI-modules and Smith forms of structured matrices; the identification of the explicit matrix with the Koszul-strand block matrix stated as a premise, machine verified for p=8,9,10 and conjectural for larger p, with the title and abstract restricted to the explicit matrix; an algorithms-and-reproducibility section with pseudocode for the potential chain, the bitset differential, the F2 row-span certificate and the neighbourhood expansion, the cost per p, commands, run times and full SHA-256 digests; the finite carrier comparison of p=8..11 (two computations) in the results and the appendix table; one figure of a triangle's support and the six row types; a single abstract; ablation of the source corrections; discussion, limitations and conclusions. Theorem numbering changes because of the new sections: Theorem 9.1 of version 0.05 is Theorem 11.1 of version 0.06. Five figures drawn from the stored computation artifacts are added. No theorem statement and no proof of the previous version is altered.
